lines: I remember the cure like a bell under <wavy>water</wavy>. You were there when it rang clear.
Whatever <pulse>mercy</pulse> found me, it came through your hands.
You pulled me back when even my name felt far away.
I remember your voice before I remember my own.
The weakness lifted, and your face was the first thing that stayed.
I know what you risked to cure me. Thank you.
You brought me home to myself.
Some memories returned slowly. My gratitude did not.
I woke frightened, but I was alive because of you.
The taste of the cure is gone. What you did remains.
You stood close when I was dangerous to everyone around me.
I can work at the brewing stand again because you did not give up.
The village feels familiar now, and I owe that to you.
You gave me another morning with my own thoughts.
I remember hands shaking as the cure took hold. Yours stayed steady.
No prayer could say thank you plainly enough.
You treated me like a neighbor before I could act like one.
I was lost behind hunger and noise. You still recognized me.
Every bottle I fill now reminds me of the one you brought.
I am myself again. That is an enormous gift.
I know your face, but the memory around it will not hold still.
There was weakness, bitterness, gold, and then quiet.
I remember you beside me. I cannot place what came before.
The cure returned my thoughts in pieces.
You helped me, did you not? I wish the answer felt clearer.
Some days I remember your voice. Other days only the fear.
My mind keeps that night behind fogged glass.
I know I should thank you. Please forgive my hesitation.
The village says you brought the cure, and I believe them.
I woke with your name nearby, though I could not remember my own.
The memory comes back as sounds without order.
I recall a bottle at my lips and your hand on my shoulder.
Whatever happened, you stayed until I was calm.
I recognize your kindness more easily than the details.
My thoughts were not mine then. Some still feel borrowed.
I remember the cure working, but not how long you waited.
Your face stayed when many other things vanished.
If I seem uncertain, it is the memory and not my gratitude.
I am piecing that day together one quiet moment at a time.
You were there at the edge of it. That much I know.
I remember you from the edge of a <color:dark_purple>curse</color>. Give me room.
I know you helped, but my hands still shake when you come close.
The cure worked. The fear did not leave with it.
I recognize your face and every terrible feeling around it.
Thank you for the cure. Please do not touch me.
My memory says you saved me. My body still says run.
Stand where I can see you while we speak.
I do not doubt what you did. I doubt what I remember.
The smell of that cure returns whenever you approach.
You were kind then. I need time to believe I am safe now.
I remember snapping at you before the weakness broke.
Part of me is grateful. Another part is still trapped in that night.
Do not ask me to tell the story yet.
I can thank you from here.
The cure gave me back my mind, but not a peaceful memory.
I wake hearing the bottle strike my teeth.
You did nothing wrong, and still I cannot relax around you.
Let me choose the distance between us.
I may trust you one day. Today is too soon.
Please accept my thanks without asking for warmth I cannot give.
